Analysis: Hypothesis 1 presents an integrative framework linking chronic inflammation, CAF‐mediated ECM stiffening, and mechanotransduction to therapy resistance. While its mechanistic elements are grounded in known biology, the high complexity and multiple overlapping pathways raise concerns regarding the clear dissection of causality and specificity. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 leverages the unique context of IDH-mutant iCCA to propose a targeted mechanism in which 2-HG induces specific epigenetic changes at cytokine promoters, thereby driving CAF activation and chemoresistance. This hypothesis is more focused with explicit endpoints (i.e., defined histone marks, promoter-specific remodeling), and proposes clear state-of-the-art methods (such as ChIP-seq, CRISPR epigenome editing, and spatial transcriptomics) to test its predictions. Although both hypotheses face challenges in establishing causality and dealing with the complexity of the tumor microenvironment, Hypothesis 2’s specificity and targeted approach increase its testability and align well with current molecular and genomic technologies. In terms of safety, both hypotheses are comparable as they primarily aim to deepen mechanistic understanding at the preclinical level. Overall, considering novelty, plausibility, testability, and safety, Hypothesis 2 demonstrates a slightly superior balance and precision.
